purpose: Neutral cross-language vectors for authenticated blocks (RFC 0006 section 3, section 5 rules (t), (u), (v)): the block header and block encodings with the appended producer and producer_signature, the 32-byte message a producer signs, strict Ed25519 verdicts for block signatures, and what a node at genesis does with each block.

authority.rfc: docs/rfcs/0006-chain-identity-authenticated-blocks.md section 3 (block format, signature, strict definition) and section 5 (rules t, u, v)
authority.implementation: crates/mbongo-core/src/primitives.rs (BlockHeader::signing_hash, Block::verify_producer_signature); crates/mbongo-node/src/backend.rs (apply_block rules t, u, v; produce_block)

conventions.header_encoding: SCALE(BlockHeader) = parent_hash (32) || state_root (32) || transactions_root (32) || timestamp (u64 LE) || height (u64 LE) || producer (32): 144 bytes
conventions.block_encoding: SCALE(Block) = SCALE(BlockHeader) || SCALE(BlockBody) || producer_signature (64). Every block here has an empty body, encoded 00
conventions.block_hash: BLAKE3(block_encoding): the whole block, the signature included
conventions.signing_hash: BLAKE3("mbongo-block:v1" || chain_id || header_encoding), the 32 bytes the producer signs
conventions.expected: valid or invalid: the strict verdict for producer_signature by header.producer over signing_hash
conventions.rule: the first requirement the signature does not meet over this chain's signing_hash, or valid
conventions.apply_block: what a node of `chain`, holding only its genesis, does with block_encoding: accepted, or the first error. Rules (t), (u), (v) are evaluated in that order after height, parent and transactions_root, and before any transaction. A valid block carries state_root(1) of an empty block, so it also passes rule (w)
conventions.keys: TEST ONLY. The dev authority seed is public: BLAKE3("mbongo:dev-authority:v1"). The other seed is 0x5c repeated

derivation.method: Derived without the Rust crates or the SDK. Ed25519: the BigInt implementation of S1-2 (RFC 8032, SHA-512 from node:crypto), checked there against RFC 8032 tests 1 to 3, OpenSSL and libsodium's small-order blocklist; every honest signature here is also produced by OpenSSL, and must be byte-identical. BLAKE3: the implementation written from its specification in S1-5. SCALE: by hand. Layout, message and rule order: read from the RFC text. state_root(0) uses the formula of state-root-v1.json, checked here against that file's genesis.
derivation.script: derive-block-signature-v1.mjs, kept with the S1-7 evidence; re-running it reproduces this file

test_keys.warning: TEST ONLY. NOT PRODUCTION KEYS. Every seed is public.

cases.name: valid-dev
cases.note: Block 1 of the dev chain, empty body, signed by the dev authority over its own chain_id.

cases.name: valid-other-chain-same-authority
cases.note: Block 1 of a second network whose genesis names the same authority key. Its timestamp equals its parent's, which rule (v) accepts.

cases.name: timestamp-at-u64-max
cases.note: Rule (v) has no upper bound (RFC 0006 §5): a timestamp of u64::MAX is valid.

cases.name: cross-chain-signature
cases.note: The dev header, signed by the same authority key over the other network's chain_id. The key is the authority of both networks; the signature is for the other one.

cases.name: whole-block-from-another-chain
cases.note: valid-dev, replayed whole on the other network: its parent is another genesis block, so it is refused before rule (t). Its signature would not verify there either.

cases.name: s-plus-group-order
cases.note: valid-dev with s replaced by s + L: the same value modulo L, so a malleable form of one signature, and one block would have two hashes.

cases.name: s-high-bit
cases.note: s with bit 255 set.

cases.name: r-identity
cases.note: R of order 1.

cases.name: r-non-canonical
cases.note: R encoding with y >= p.

cases.name: r-not-a-point
cases.note: R bytes that decode to no curve point.

cases.name: cofactored-equation-only
cases.note: Satisfies the cofactored equation only: R carries a torsion component.

cases.name: signature-over-another-header
cases.note: An honest signature over the same header with timestamp + 1: the signature covers the whole header.

cases.name: signature-over-the-preimage
cases.note: Signed over "mbongo-block:v1" || chain_id || SCALE(header) itself, not its BLAKE3: the signed message is the 32-byte hash.

cases.name: signature-without-domain
cases.note: Signed over BLAKE3(chain_id || SCALE(header)): the domain is part of the message.

cases.name: signature-with-the-transaction-domain
cases.note: Signed over BLAKE3("mbongo-tx:v2" || chain_id || SCALE(header)): another protocol domain.

cases.name: zero-signature
cases.note: The genesis block's zero signature on block 1. R = 0x00..00 decodes to a point of small order.

cases.name: authority-named-another-key-signs
cases.note: A forged block: the header names the authority, and another key signs the right message.

cases.name: unauthorized-producer-valid-signature
cases.note: A forged block: another key names itself producer and signs correctly. Its signature is strictly valid; the producer is not the authority.

cases.name: unauthorized-zero-producer
cases.note: Block 1 with the genesis block's zero producer and zero signature: rule (t) refuses it first.

cases.name: unauthorized-small-order-producer
cases.note: A producer key of order 1, with a signature satisfying the equation for it. Rule (t) refuses it before any key check.

cases.name: timestamp-below-parent
cases.note: A validly signed block one second before its parent (the other genesis, timestamp 1700000000).

cases.name: timestamp-zero-below-parent
cases.note: A validly signed block at timestamp 0 on a genesis at 1700000000.

cases.name: bad-signature-and-bad-timestamp
cases.note: Fails rules (u) and (v): (u) is reported, it comes first.

cases.name: unauthorized-and-bad-signature-and-bad-timestamp
cases.note: Fails rules (t), (u) and (v): (t) is reported, it comes first.
